EMG shows low CMAPs that increase in amplitude with repetitive stimulation (incremental response), which is diagnostic for Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS). Elevated voltage-gated P/Q-type calcium channel antibodies further support LEMS. Autonomic findings (dry mucous membranes, sluggish pupils) are commonly seen in LEMS. The patient’s long heavy smoking history, cough, and weight loss raise high suspicion for an underlying small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), the most frequent paraneoplastic cause of LEMS; a normal chest X-ray does not rule out an occult SCLC, so chest CT and oncologic evaluation are indicated.

DIAGNOSIS: Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (paraneoplastic, most likely secondary to small cell lung carcinoma)
